observations: Photo 0 shows a black Canon DSLR camera with a lens attached, placed on artificial grass. The camera body has 'Canon' and 'EOS 750D' clearly visible on the top. A lens cap with 'Canon' is also present.
Photo 1 shows the same camera inside an orange and black zippered case, with accessories like a battery, charger, and strap visible. The camera is secured in the case.
The camera appears to be in used condition with some visible wear on the body and lens cap.
No screen, sensor, or internal components are visible in either photo.

The seller's text claims it is a 'Canon EOS 750D (Rebel T6i)' with 24.2-megapixel APS-C DSLR, released in 2015, shutter count under 5,000, no fungus or scratch on the lens, original battery and charger, never repaired.

claims.claim: Canon EOS 750D (Rebel T6i) is a 24.2-megapixel APS-C DSLR camera, released in 2015
claims.evidence: The model name 'EOS 750D' is visible in photo 0, but 'Rebel T6i' is not visible on the camera body. The 24.2-megapixel claim is not verifiable from the photos. The 2015 release year is not visible.

claims.claim: Shutter count under 5,000, no fungus or scratch on the lens. Original battery and charger, never repaired.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: Lens may be damaged or non-functional (e.g., scratches, fungus, or internal issues)
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the lens glass and front element, and a test photo taken with the lens.

risks.risk: Battery or charger may be missing or non-functional
risks.proof: Photo of the battery and charger, and a video showing them charging and powering the camera.
risks.if_unproven: priced as missing battery and charger

Close-up photo of the lens glass and front element.
Photo of the battery and charger, and a video showing them charging and powering the camera.
Photo of the camera sensor and body interior.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
